text:
Maria: Pinging for design sync — prototyping autoshard/warmup for safetensors bundles. Main Q: do we require full checksum before any use, or allow streaming+background-verify?

Ashish: leaning toward streaming start once manifest/header validated. Do background checksum and have rollback (evict+fallback) if it fails.

Kai: manifest must be source-of-truth. Per-shard sha256 + byte ranges + manifest sig. Loader verifies manifest sig before streaming.

Jeremy: propose model flags: "fast_start": true|false, "verify_mode": "blocking"|"background"|"deferred". Default background for large (>1GB) models.

Maria: example manifest I sketched:
```
{"model":"sofa-7b","version":"v2","manifest_version":2,"shards":[{"idx":0,"size":12345678,"sha256":"abcd..."},{"idx":1,"size":9876543,"sha256":"1234..."}],"streaming":{"verify":"background","atomic_update":true}}
```

Ashish: key question: if verify=background, do we allow shard parts to be used for generation before checksum completes? If yes, restrict to KV-prefetch only; no generation until verified.

Kai: agree — two-tier access: prefix/kv warmup allowed, but autoregeneration gated until verified or fallback active.

Jeremy: edge cases: overlapping shard ranges, partial reuploads during rolling upgrade, duplicate shard ids with different checksums. Treat idx+sha mismatch as fatal and trigger manifest rollback.

Ashish: Ops: CI must compute and attach manifest sig. ci-bot: can we add a pipeline job that fails on missing per-shard checksum?

ci-bot: noted. I'll add a release workflow job to compute safetensors-manifest and validate signatures; failures will block release.

Maria: Perf tradeoffs note: blocking verify adds startup tail (~1-3s per GB). Background verify + gated generation reduces tail but increases complexity. I'll draft RFC with perf numbers and a failure state machine (evict->fallback->alert). Plan: manifest-first, background-verify default with gated generation, explicit rollback path, CI enforced manifests. Opening PR today, pinging reviewers.
